claims.what: **Twelve people of the name are documented in Carnia itself**, across three villages. The origin the family always asserted now rests on record rather than on Carlo's word alone.

The **Napoleonic civil registers of the Comune di Mione** — fifty-nine volumes at the Archivio di Stato di Udine, which nobody had opened — give **five De Franceschi households and eight deaths at Mione and Muina, 1806–1810**.
The marriage *allegati* push the Mione family back to a **Giovanni Battista de' Franceschi already dead by 1789** — and both of the forenames Carlo gave for his own ancestors are in that valley.
**Agrons.** Three independent sources arriving within an hour of each other answered the question this archive was built to ask: *where* in Carnia.
The headmen's return of **1679** was a list of **weavers on the road of the Furlans** — Ferigo's scholarship supplies the mechanism that the family tradition only asserted.
Dean Brhan's studies of the Carnia-to-Istria migration **name this family twice**, in the one body of scholarship that has actually examined this movement.
A **third Carnian household of the name stood at Svetvinčenat**, with a *Stanzia De Franceschi* on the cadastre of 1820 — forty kilometres south, and never looked for.
Puhmajer's published statement that **Gologorica and Seget are two branches of one family** is contested here, with the reasons set out.

**Carlo's own published history of Istria never makes the Carnia claim.** The word appears twice in 524 pages, neither time about his family. The testimony rests entirely on a private letter and his memoirs.

cannot: **No document yet joins any Carnian household to the Gologorica family.** The origin is established; the descent is not.
The **Ovaro parish registers before 1806** are in no portal and must be asked for from the parish.
The *gismani* charters cannot be read outside one private house and one box in Trieste.

claims.what: **1661 — the first time the name is written in this village**, found in a single clause of a 2022 article about the family's book collection.
**Eighty-eight people of the surname** stand in the Gologorica and Gračišće household books between **1785 and 1945**, in nine households, read frame by frame.
The parish priest **Ljudevit Žváček kept a chronicle from 1892 to 1923** — the village seen from inside, by a Czech recruited through an advertisement in a Prague newspaper.
The house carries **a coat of arms**: Matejčić's 1979 survey of Istrian Baroque has the family raising its *palazzetto* with an arcaded portico and a blazon on the front.
**Carlo De Franceschi's grave** is in his own village's cemetery, as *Il giovine Pensiero* wrote in 1893 — and the family has now stood in it and photographed the stone.
**Six households in 1820**, from the Franciscan cadastre — and one of them is entered *«di Gallignana»*.
The village's speech was **recorded in 1930** in a Kraków dialect atlas; both of this family's parishes are survey points in it.
A marriage at **Valle, 22 January 1795** — a hundred kilometres down the west coast, found in a study of that parish's registers.
**Nothing yet joins the Gologorica house to the Gallignana line** of farmers and stonecutters two villages away. Both families believe they are one; no record says so.

cannot: **The join to Gallignana** — the single question this page exists around, and it is still open.
Whose the arms on the house actually are, and by what right they were put there.
What the family was doing at Gologorica between the first mention in **1661** and the household books that begin in **1785**.
